archetype: Mono-black aristocrats-combo, and the frame agrees. strategic_frame.json calls it 'a sacrifice engine that draws while it assembles and closes with one of four rules-verified drain loops'; deck-audit matches the archetype to combo off that frame and prices tutors and protection against the combo band. The 28 creatures are fodder and outlets, not a beatdown plan — the deck's only wincon:combat card is Mikaeus, the Unhallowed.
verdict: This deck's functional layer is finished: 36 lands, 42 black sources against a Karsten target of 36, two unconditional taplands, and a 0.919 turn-three land-drop rate. Its enabler layer is finished too — drain 82.4%, sac outlet 77.9%, fodder 73.6%, ignition 73.1% — which is the layer strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density says fails first, and here it does not. What limits it is interaction-breadth, and specifically one hole: Feed the Swarm is the only card in the 99 that can destroy or exile a noncreature permanent an opponent controls (Blasting Station can damage a planeswalker; nothing else reaches one), and it cannot touch an artifact. Fourteen cards in the 99 need the graveyard and, read from oracle text, three of the four verified kills stop under a static graveyard lock — so a resolved Grafdigger's Cage is a permanent the deck has no answer to at all.

add_candidates.why: Two mana, mono-black, and it is repeatable artifact removal whose cost is a creature the deck wants dead anyway — every activation is a drain trigger. It takes the artifact class from zero answers to one and the 'answer to a noncreature permanent' component from one card to two. The enumeration behind the pick, re-run and corrected. Filtering data/cards.csv for Commander-legal nonland cards whose colour identity is a subset of mono-black, at mana value four or less, whose oracle text destroys or exiles a TARGET artifact or permanent — or all, or each, of them — returns thirty-nine, none already in the 99 or on the bench. The previous run of this filter reported thirty-six and was wrong in both directions: it matched 'artifact' and 'permanent' as unbounded substrings, which admitted Tsabo's Assassin (it destroys only creatures; 'permanents' appears there only in a colour-counting clause), and it dropped four cards that satisfy the stated filter verbatim — Aetherjacket, Despotic Scepter, Synod Sanctum and Staff of Compleation. The thirty-nine partition exhaustively, and the partition sums. Three answer an opponent's artifact repeatably from the battlefield with no combat, graveyard or ownership gate: Gate to Phyrexia, Lux Cannon, Culling Scales. Twelve are symmetric mass destruction (Nevinyrral's Disk, Oblivion Stone, Ratchet Bomb, Powder Keg, Perilous Vault, Karn's Sylex, The Filigree Sylex, Boompile, Coercive Portal, Eye of Doom, Engineered Explosives, The Moment). Eight are one-shots behind a five-to-seven-mana activation (Unstable Obelisk, which does destroy any permanent, plus Goblin Firebomb, Universal Solvent, Thaumaton Torpedo, Lunatic Pandora, Boom Box, Bumbleflower's Sharepot, Clay Golem). Two are one-shots at a cost this deck can actually pay: Aetherjacket and Phyrexian Tribute. Three only exile artifact cards from graveyards (Myr Welder, Conversion Chamber, Grave Robbers). Two are gated on combat damage or on entering from a graveyard (Sword of Sinew and Steel, Canoptek Tomb Sentinel — and a graveyard-gated answer is the wrong answer to a graveyard lock). Five reach only permanents you own or control (Despotic Scepter, Staff of Compleation, Synod Sanctum, Rats of Rath, Wirefly Hive). Four cannot point at a colourless artifact like Grafdigger's Cage at all: Aligned Hedron Network reaches only creatures, Apocalypse Chime only cards first printed in Homelands, Null Elemental Blast only multicoloured permanents, and Eldrazi Confluence's exile returns the permanent to the battlefield. Two rivals, both real. Lux Cannon is broader — 'Destroy target permanent' reaches any permanent type, so it closes two of the three uncovered classes, artifact and land, against Gate's one — but it costs {4}, then three untaps before its first activation and three more between each one after, and it is itself an artifact in front of the opponent playing artifacts. Aetherjacket is the omission that bears hardest on the pick, and it is not a throwaway: a {3} 2/1 flier whose '{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this creature: Destroy another target artifact' makes its own cost a death trigger for the nine-card drain component, and whose body the fodder component can use — the same argument this entry makes for Gate. It loses on three counts, not one: it is one-shot where Gate is repeatable, it is sorcery-speed only and must survive a turn to pay the {T}, and its two halves cost five mana between them against Gate's two. Culling Scales cannot be steered — it destroys the lowest-mana-value nonland permanent each upkeep, which here is the deck's own 0-mana tokens, then Sol Ring and Skullclamp. So the pick is speed and repeatability over breadth, and the threat decides it: the permanent this diagnosis names as unanswerable, Grafdigger's Cage, is an artifact, and three turns of Lux Cannon charging under a graveyard lock is a lost game. The upkeep-only, once-each-turn restriction is Gate's own price. It comes in for Supernatural Stamina, this document's easy cut: a duplicated protection copy traded for an uncovered class, which is the order strategy:deckbuilding.cutting sets. Protection goes from six real copies to five, inside the 4–6 band, and the deck keeps one instant-speed save for a targeted Yawgmoth.

gaps: deck_recon.json (as_of 2026-08-03) has drifted from the current decklist (sha256 61868aea…). It states that Marauding Blight-Priest is 'absent from the 99' and that Exquisite Blood 'has no partner in the 99 that turns it into a kill' — both are false; it lists Blowfly Infestation among cards the deck runs, and cards.json does not; and it says Cabal Coffers and Urborg are flagged is_sideboard, when both are in the maindeck. Its inclusion percentages are cited here for two cards the deck does not run (Withering Torment, Pawn of Ulamog) and for one it does: Supernatural Stamina at 6.7%, taken from the recon's own 'this deck DOES run' block, which the drift above does not touch. A re-run would settle it.
No per-commander inclusion rate exists in any local artifact. Every percentage in this diagnosis that did not come from deck-audit came from deck_recon.json and carries its date.
bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so deck-audit could not confirm it is current for this list. The power axis figure is carried as reported.

There is no measured 'any kill assembled' rate. goldfish_targets.json states that its AND-of-ORs schema cannot express the union of four independent kills, so the deck's true conversion rate is higher than any of 1.1%, 0.5%, 6.9% or 4.6% and is unmeasured. This diagnosis therefore does not call conversion the binding axis.

The deck's exposure to creature-ability hosers (Cursed Totem, Torpor Orb) is unpriced: at least eight of the deck's creatures carry battlefield activated abilities (Yawgmoth, Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Woe Strider, Ayara, Warren Soultrader, Yahenni, Fume Spitter), but no artifact enumerates which of the deck's functions are creature-activated versus artifact- or enchantment-activated.

Gate to Phyrexia did not come from any of upgrade-facts' three evidence channels — it came from an enumeration of data/cards.csv (Commander-legal, colour identity within mono-black or colourless, nonland, mana value ≤ 4, oracle text destroying or exiling a target artifact or permanent, or all or each of them, matched on whole words) which returns thirty-nine candidates. Its EDHREC rank is 15,886, so this is a fit argument rather than a consensus one, and the choice of it over Lux Cannon (broader, slower) and Aetherjacket (a body and a death trigger, but one-shot) is a judgement about speed against breadth that no artifact in this repo prices.

This cut list carries no `painful` entry, and that is a finding rather than a dodge. The one painful cut this document proposed was Necropotence, and it is withdrawn on three counts. Its arithmetic was wrong: eleven maindeck entries in cards.json say 'draw' and one of them is the commander, so the 99 holds ten draw sources and cutting one lands on nine — below the template floor of ten, on an axis deck-audit already reads `under`. Its 'duplicated function' premise is false against the cards: reading all ten, the other nine are each gated on a body (Skullclamp, Ayara, Deadly Dispute, Plumb the Forbidden, Sinister Gnarlbark), on mana and a tap (Castle Locthwain), on a once-per-turn cap (Black Market Connections), on being a one-shot spell (Insatiable Avarice) or on an opponent (Massacre Girl), while Necropotence is uncapped, body-free and mana-free — and this deck's checker-passed stacks 009 and 011 make life its cheapest currency, which makes it uniquely good here rather than duplicated. And it orphans tutor_guide.json's scripted fetch for the board where Yawgmoth has been answered. No replacement painful cut is offered: the 99 was not re-searched for a third candidate at this pass, and substituting one unreviewed at the final iteration is how a prescription ships unchecked. Whether this deck has a painful cut at all is open.

findings.note: Protection is counted as six by including the commander, contradicting this document's own convention four axes earlier. axes[5] subtracts Yawgmoth explicitly ('one of the eleven is the commander, who is not in the 99, so the 99 itself holds ten'); axes[8] adds him back ('the audit's probe adds Yawgmoth's own protection from Humans ... That is six'). The 99 holds five: Lightning Greaves, Sedgemoor Witch, Yahenni, Malakir Rebirth, Supernatural Stamina (oracle text of all five re-read; Malakir Rebirth and Supernatural Stamina are the same death-replacement clause, confirmed verbatim from cards.csv; deck-audit lists Yawgmoth only under possible_uncounted). This propagates verbatim into cut_candidates[1].cost_of_cutting and add_candidates[0].why, which both state 'Protection drops from six real copies to five, still inside the 4-6 band'. Counting the 99 only, the cut of Supernatural Stamina lands protection at FOUR — the exact floor of deck-audit's operative 4-6 combo band, not mid-band. NO CITED FLOOR IS BROKEN and the prescription survives: 4 is inside 4-6. But the axis's own citation block quotes Zupke's '5-7 protection slots', under which four is below floor, and the entire content of cut_candidates[1].cost_of_cutting is the margin claim that is off by one.
